title: Accessibility stabilization: token contrast, keyboard focus, and VPAT readiness
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Summary: Run a focused accessibility stabilization pass across core design-system primitives (color tokens, interactive buttons, table rows, and chart legends) to ensure VPAT readiness. This ticket covers audit remediation for WCAG contrast failures, inconsistent focus outlines/keyboard navigation, and updating token semantics so runtime mapping (dark/light) does not break A11y. Goal: ship a small set of deterministic fixes that unblock the upcoming VPAT review and reduce a11y regressions in product releases.
proposed_design_changes: Introduce semantic foreground/background tokens (e.g., fg/neutral/interactive-strong) and map existing brand tokens to them to preserve contrast targets.

Standardize focus ring implementation across buttons, inputs, and table rows using a 3px visible outline with non-invasive offset; add utility token for focus-color that meets 3:1 with surrounding UI.
Add keyboard-action affordances for table row expansion/selection (Enter/Space) and ensure row-hover styles are not the only indicator of focus state.
Update chart legend items to include role=button where interactive, provide aria-pressed for toggle states, and ensure colorblind-safe markers by pairing color with shape or pattern tokens.
Document exceptions where 4.5:1 cannot be met (small text/branding) and include rationale and compensating measures in the VPAT appendix.
acceptance_criteria: All updated tokens have a semantics table and mapping notes in the token spec page.
Contrast analyzer run shows no new WCAG AA contrast failures for updated components when tested on primary light/dark themes.
Keyboard navigation tests pass: tab order, visible focus, Enter/Space activation for interactive rows and controls.
VPAT draft has been updated with changes and marked Ready for Legal review.
Design tokens and component changes are covered by at least one unit/integration test or visual regression test.
qa_checklist: Run automated axe-core scan on example pages (buttons, tables, charts) — attach report.
Manual keyboard walkthroughs (mac/Windows) for navigation and action activation — attach session notes.
Contrast verification using Color Contrast Analyzer for top 5 most-used screens.
Figma prototypes updated with focus styles and token names; handoff tokens to platform team.
Smoke test in staging with Dedicated and Hosted themes to validate runtime token mappings.
decisions: Use semantic token layer instead of renaming all brand tokens to avoid large migration churn for product teams.
Adopt visible focus ring as default across interactive primitives; allow opt-out via 'reduced-focus' token for specific UIs that need different visuals.
Avoid forcing 4.5:1 for brand-logo text; treat those as documented exceptions in VPAT with compensating alt text and non-color cues.
progress_updates: 2025-01-20: Kickoff review with Platform and Frontend Eng. Inventory of affected components completed (buttons, primary table, chart legend).
2025-01-24: Token spec draft created in Confluence; initial semantic token mapping proposed. UX edge-case meeting scheduled to discuss focus stroke thickness.
2025-01-29: Prototypes in Figma updated; UX sign-off on focus ring style. Started PR for tokens-to-css-vars mapping (github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/482).
2025-02-02: Axe automated run shows 18 initial failures reduced to 3 after token adjustments. Filing follow-ups for those three that require engineering changes to DOM structure.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Reyes): Request to include a short rollback plan for token changes and communicate to product teams in next alpha release notes.
Engineering (Priya Singh): Raised concern about large bundle churn if we ship new token variables without migration; suggested a legacy alias layer for 2 release cycles.
Accessibility consultant (external): Suggested adding non-color indicators for chart legends and avoiding color-only focus cues for dense tables.
Legal: Asked for a VPAT section that explains testing matrix (browser/OS/contrast tool versions) and known limitations.
